.github/workflows/publish-release.yml: # Guarded release controller. A `v*` tag builds the sdist and wheel in a read-only job, then
# a separate job holding the write scopes attests and publishes exactly the files the build
# job produced. workflow_dispatch and changes to this file or its helper run the build job
# alone (a dry run that never publishes), so the release path is exercised before the
# This file replaces .github/workflows/release.yml. A tag push runs the workflow file found
# at the tagged commit, so every older commit's release.yml still publishes a matching tag
# without the provenance check; that legacy path must be disabled in the repository's
# Actions settings (SSDLC.md, "Enforced controls"), and tools/check_workflow_policy.py keeps
# the path from coming back so disabling it never disables this controller.
# Per ref: a dry run or a re-run of one tag never cancels that ref's run in flight. Different
# tags get different groups here, so the publish job carries its own constant group below.
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
# The provenance and release checks run in a fresh job of pinned actions and these two
# steps only, so no earlier step and no repository test can change the PATH or the
# environment their `gh` and `python` run under (the runner's file commands carry such
# changes to later steps of the same job). tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins
# this whole job: keys, permissions, runner and every step, in order.
contents: read   # checkout and the compare API for the provenance check
actions: read    # the tagged commit's workflow runs for the release checks gate
- name: Check out the commit being released
- name: A release tag must point at a commit already on main
# Tag protection is not enforceable on this plan (SSDLC.md), so the workflow checks it:
# compare/<sha>...main is "identical" or "ahead" only when main contains the commit.
# A tag fails closed on any other answer; dry runs report only. The pull-request head,
# not GitHub's synthetic merge commit, is what a dry run compares.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins this step's env and run lines exactly.
- name: The tagged commit's ci and CodeQL workflows must have passed
# Required checks are not enforceable on this plan (SSDLC.md), and the build job re-runs
# the test gate but not CodeQL. Only push runs of ci.yml and codeql.yml (by workflow path)
# for this exact commit count, never a job name another workflow could reuse; a tag
# fails closed on a missing, pending or failed run; dry runs report only.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 4 pins this step's env and run lines exactly.

gh api --paginate "repos/${GH_REPO}/actions/runs?head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=100" --jq '.workflow_runs[] | {path, name, event, status, conclusion, head_sha, updated_at}' > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/workflow-runs.jsonl" || echo "api-error" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/workflow-runs.jsonl"
# Read-only: the gate, the version check, the distributions, the wheel smoke, the SBOM
# and the checksums. Nothing in this job can write to the repository.
name: release build (gate, version check, distributions, SBOM, checksums)
- name: The full gate must pass on the commit being released
- name: The reported version must equal pyproject.toml, and the tag when there is one
DECLARED=$(python -c 'import re; print(re.search(r"^version = \"([^\"]+)\"", open("pyproject.toml", encoding="utf-8").read(), re.M).group(1))')
test "${VERSION}" = "${DECLARED}" || (echo "protodetect reports ${VERSION} but pyproject.toml declares ${DECLARED}" && exit 1)
test "v${VERSION}" = "${TAG}" || (echo "tag ${TAG} does not match version ${VERSION}" && exit 1)
- name: The runner's gh supports every attestation flag the publish job verifies with
# The publish job only runs for a real tag; this dry-runnable check keeps an image change
# from first surfacing as a failed release.
grep -q -- "$flag" <<<"$HELP" || { echo "$(gh --version) lacks gh attestation verify $flag"; exit 1; }
echo "gh attestation verify flags present" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
- name: Build distributions, check and smoke the wheel, SBOM and checksums
- name: Hand the exact files to the publish job
# Only a pushed `v*` tag reaches this job; dry runs stop after the build. It checks out
# nothing: it attests and publishes the build job's files after re-verifying their checksums.
# One constant group for every tag: publishes of different tags never overlap, and one in
# flight is never cancelled. GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so a third tag pushed
# while one publishes and another waits replaces the waiting one, which ends cancelled
# (nothing published) and is re-run by hand. tools/check_workflow_policy.py enforces this.
contents: write       # gh release create uploads the distributions to the release
id-token: write       # OIDC token for the Sigstore signing of the provenance attestation
attestations: write   # attest-build-provenance stores the attestation on the repository
- name: Fetch the build job's files
- name: The files must still match the checksums the build job recorded
- name: Every file's attestation must verify before anything is published
# Binds each file to this controller workflow, this tag and commit, and a GitHub-hosted
# runner; a missing or partial attestation fails the release before gh release create.
# tools/check_workflow_policy.py rule 8 pins every step of this job, in order (an allowlist).
- name: Publish the release with the runner's gh CLI (no third-party action)
.github/workflows/release-audit.yml: # Scheduled release audit: a detective control no tag can bypass. A tag push runs the workflow
# file at the tagged commit, so an older commit's unguarded release.yml (or a workflow edited on
# a branch) can still publish; a scheduled run always uses the default branch's copy of this
# file. It fails, and GitHub notifies the owner, when a v* tag points off main or a published
# release is not bound to a current, on-main v* tag and its commit, or has an asset (hidden files
# included) without an attestation from publish-release.yml for that tag and commit. Read-only.
# Schedules only run from the default branch, so this takes effect once merged to main; pushes
# that change it run it as a dry run against the real releases. See SSDLC.md.
# Explicit bash runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`; the unspecified default is
# `bash -e` without pipefail, under which a failing check piped into tee passes the step.
name: release audit (v* tags on main, every asset attested by the controller)
contents: read       # list tags and releases, compare refs, download release assets
attestations: read   # gh attestation verify reads the repository's attestations
- name: Gather facts about every v* tag and published release, then decide
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg compare "$status" --arg commit "$commit" '{kind: "tag", tag: $tag, compare: $compare, commit: $commit}' >> "$facts"
if gh release download "$tag" --dir "$dir"; then download=ok; else download=error; fi
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg commit "$commit" --arg download "$download" --argjson assets "$count" '{kind: "release", tag: $tag, commit: $commit, assets: $assets, download: $download}' >> "$facts"

if gh attestation verify "$file" --repo "$GH_REPO" --signer-workflow "$GH_REPO/.github/workflows/publish-release.yml" --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" --source-digest "$commit" --deny-self-hosted-runners > /dev/null; then verified=true; else verified=false; fi
jq -nc --arg tag "$tag" --arg asset "$(basename "$file")" --argjson verified "$verified" '{kind: "asset", tag: $tag, asset: $asset, verified: $verified}' >> "$facts"
